The description does not record which voltage variant this specific valve instance was ordered with, but both 24 V DC and 230 V AC are supported variants, so 24 V DC will work if the valve is fitted with the 24V DC coil; otherwise you would need the 230V AC coil version. Also note it runs on AC or DC depending on variant, with power consumption of about 5 W (DC) or 11 VA operation / 20 VA inrush (AC).

final.answer: The valve operated by control loop FIC-2-1 is FV-2-1, a globe valve. Its datasheet lists these seal materials for the valve plug seal (Table 14, pages 20-21): carbon-filled PTFE (2-piece seal, standard for NPS 1-6 valves without Cavitrol III cage) rated -73 °C/-100 °F to 232 °C/450 °F; ethylene-propylene rated -40 °C/-40 °F to 232 °C/450 °F (not for petroleum-based fluids and hydrocarbons); fluorocarbon rated -18 °C/0 °F to 204 °C/400 °F (not for steam or ammonia, not for water above 82 °C/180 °F); nitrile rated -40 °C/-40 °F to 71 °C/160 °F for air and hydrocarbons (or up to 82 °C/180 °F for other compatible fluids; not with fire-resistant hydraulic oils); PTFE with N10276 spring (spring-loaded seal, standard for NPS 8 valves and NPS 1-6 valves with Cavitrol III cages) rated -73 °C/-100 °F to 232 °C/450 °F; and PTFE/graphite with R30003 spring plus PEEK anti-extrusion rings rated -73 °C/-100 °F to 316 °C/600 °F, but limited to 260 °C/500 °F in oxidizing service. The metal parts (backup/retaining rings, springs, S41600 stainless parts, PEEK rings) are described as not limiting for temperature, except the S41600 stainless parts of the spring-loaded seal, which have a minimum of -29 °C/-20 °F. A part literally called a piston ring does not appear in the datasheet; the closest items are the plug seal rings and the PEEK anti-extrusion rings.
